# Lang Module Guide

_Author: Zach Bogart, Brayden Youngberg_
_Version: 3.0.0_

## Overview

The `Lang` module provides a set of helper functions to manage translations, template insertions, and string formatting in JavaScript notebooks and apps. It is especially useful for multi-language support and dynamic text replacement.

---

## Installation & Defining Languages

Define available languages with keys, labels, and locales:
```{ojs}
import { lang as Lang } from "/helpers/lang.js"

languages = [
  { key: "en", label: "English", locale: "en-US" },
  { key: "fr", label: "Français", locale: "fr-FR" }
];
```

## Setting Up Translation JSON

Structure your translations as a nested object or external JSON, with language keys for each field:

```{ojs}
nbText = new Object({
  "hello": {
    "en": "hello",
    "fr": "Bonjour"
  },
  "error": {
    "en": "Whoops"
  },
  "insert": {
    "small": {
      "en": "This is an insertion example: :::field:::",
      "fr": "Ceci est un exemple d'insertion: :::field:::"
    },
    "big": {
      "en": "This is an insertion example: :::field::: :::name:::",
      "fr": "Ceci est un exemple d'insertion: :::field::: :::name:::"
    }
  }
})
```

## Language State

Don't build a toggle per notebook. The navbar switcher
(`components/langSwitcher.js`) owns language state site-wide, and notebooks
get `language` / `_lang` from the `/components/_lang.qmd` include (see
*Notebook Content Layout* below). For the standalone examples on this page we
simply pin it:

```{ojs}
language = ({ key: "en" })
```

## Retrieving Translations

Get a translation for the current language:

```{ojs}
Lang.getText(nbText.hello, { key: language.key });
```

### Shorthand Helper

To avoid repeating the language key, use `lg`:

```{ojs}
_lang = Lang.lg(language.key);
_lang(nbText.hello); // "hello" or "Bonjour"
```


## Template Insertion

Replace placeholders in template strings with dynamic values.

### Example: Single Insertion

```{ojs}
{
    const template = Lang.getText(nbText.insert.small, { key: language.key });
    const items = [{ name: "field", value: "hello world!" }];
    return Lang.reduceReplaceTemplateItems(template, items);
}
```


### Example: Multiple Insertions

```{ojs}
{
    const template = Lang.getText(nbText.insert.big, { key: language.key });
    const greeting = Lang.getText(nbText.hello, { key: language.key });
    const items = [
    { name: "field", value: greeting },
    { name: "name", value: "Alice" }
    ];
    return Lang.reduceReplaceTemplateItems(template, items);
}
```


### Custom Placeholder Delimiters

```{ojs}
{
    const customTemplate = "This is a test: >field<";
    const result = Lang.reduceReplaceTemplateItems(
        customTemplate,
        [{ name: "field", value: "hello world!" }],
        { start: ">", end: "<" }
    );
    return result
}
```

## Checking for Missing Translations

Find missing language keys in your text object:

```{ojs}

Lang.listLeavesMissingObjectKeys(nbText, ["en", "fr"]);
// Returns an array of paths to missing translations
```

## String Formatting Helpers

```{ojs}
Lang.toTitleCase("welcome to my home");    // "Welcome To My Home"
Lang.toSentenceCase("welcome to my home"); // "Welcome to my home"
```


---

## API Reference

| Function | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| `lg(defaultKey)` | Returns a function to fetch text for a default language key. |
| `getText(textObj, { key })` | Gets text for the specified language key. |
| `parseBlock(markdown)` | Parses CMS prose and its optional collapsible note. |
| `getRegexForNamedInsertion(item, opts)` | Returns regex to match placeholders (default: `:::item:::`). |
| `reduceReplaceTemplateItems(...)` | Replaces all placeholders in a template with provided values. |
| `listLeavesMissingObjectKeys(obj, keys)` | Lists object leaves missing specified keys. |
| `getParamFromList({ name, list, ... })` | Returns query parameter value if it exists in a provided list. |
| `toTitleCase(str)` | Converts a string to title case. |
| `toSentenceCase(str)` | Converts a string to sentence case. |

---

## Notebook Content Layout (CMS)

Notebook text lives in `data/<notebook>/text/`:

- `<id>.en.md`, `<id>.fr.md` — one file per narrative **block**. The filename is the
  block id; the file contains a `title`, an optional nested `details` note, and the
  main markdown body:

  ```markdown
  ---
  title: "Overview"
  details:
    title: "How to interpret these indicators"
    body: |-
      **Indicator** — A concise definition and interpretation.
  ---

  Understanding the economic impacts...
  ```

  Notebooks place a block with the `prose` shortcode, using the block id:

  ```markdown
  {{{< prose overview >}}}

  {{{< prose costs level=2 >}}}

  {{{< prose overview-closing heading=false >}}}
  ```

  **Developers control heading level and placement in the `.qmd`; authors control the
  displayed text in the block file.** The shortcode
  (`scripts/build/proseShortcode.lua`) emits a section heading titled from the
  block's `title:` (`level=N` sets the heading level, default 1) followed by the
  block body; `heading=false` injects just the body, for free-floating blocks — for
  example an `overview-closing` block placed after a figure. Optional details can
  be rendered directly in OJS with `sections[id].details.title` and
  `sections[id].details.body`, keeping the dropdown copy in its parent CMS entry.
  Blocks can also be consumed directly in OJS code via
  `sections["indicator-definitions"]`. A shortcode pointing at a missing or empty
  block **fails the render**, and CI flags block files that nothing references (a
  typo'd id would otherwise fail silently). Default-language prose is static HTML —
  crawlable and visible before OJS boots. At runtime, `Lang.applyTranslations()`
  swaps headings and `.nb-prose` blocks when the language toggle changes (blocks are
  parsed with `Lang.parseBlock`), and restores the built English on toggle back.
- `en.json`, `fr.json` — page title (`meta.title`), widget labels, tooltips, and
  templated sentences. Identical key trees; missing keys fall back to English at
  runtime via `Lang.withFallback`.

`scripts/build/checkTranslations.ts` (run in CI) enforces the whole contract: JSON key
  parity, every block present in every locale, valid ids and front matter, non-empty
  titles and details, and every block referenced by a `.qmd` actually existing.

The narrative blocks are editable in the browser at `/admin/` (Sveltia CMS,
configured in `admin/config.yml` — one folder collection per notebook; authors can
edit but not create or delete blocks). The optional “Collapsible note” editor stores
its heading and content in the same localized file as the parent section. Edits are
committed to the repo and published by the normal build. The JSON strings are
deliberately *not* in the CMS — their keys are coupled to notebook code, so they are
edited in the repo through review. See `notebooks/cis/notebook.qmd` for a details
example and `notebooks/roi/notebook.qmd` for the base implementation.

Language state itself is owned by a vanilla navbar switcher
(`components/langSwitcher.js`) that works before the OJS runtime boots.
Notebooks pull the whole shared setup — the switcher script plus the
`Lang`/`general_translations`/`languages`/`langKey`/`language`/`_lang` OJS
cells — with a single include of `/components/_lang.qmd` (see the top of that
file for the shortcode syntax), and must not redefine those cells.
